How to use Peel

For founders and small teams who built an app with Lovable, Bolt, v0, Base44 or Cursor and store real users' data: emails, bookings, messages, payments.

Open Peel ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Open the Peel Security page and run the exposure check: five questions, nothing is sent.

2

Read the risks it lists; each matches a finding class Peel tests by hand.

3

Review the seven finding classes.

4

Choose a tier: the free snapshot, or the audit for the full manual test.

5

Send the booking form. Scope and a fixed quote come back within one business day.

02

Features

01

Exposure check

Five questions about your backend, tables, access rules, admin key and headers. Returns a score and the likely risks.

STEPS

  1. Choose your backend
  2. Answer yes or no
  3. Read the score and the risks
02

Finding classes

Missing access rules, exposed admin key, broken object-level access, over-exposed personal data, open Firebase rules, no rate limiting, weak security headers.

STEPS

  1. Read each class and its severity
  2. Check whether your app could be affected
  3. Fix it or book a test
03

Pricing

Free same-day snapshot, a flat-price audit, a comprehensive test for apps that handle money or personal data, and a monthly retainer. Every tier includes a retest.

STEPS

  1. Start with the snapshot if unsure
  2. Choose the audit for one app and its backend
  3. Add the retainer if you ship every week
04

Operator console

A dashboard of engagements, each with its risk score and progress.

STEPS

  1. Create the engagement
  2. Record the signed authorization
  3. Track the risk score
05

Checklist and findings

A checklist for AI-built apps from scoping to exploitation. Findings are scored with CVSS 3.1 and carry evidence.

STEPS

  1. Complete each check
  2. Log findings with their CVSS vector and evidence
  3. Mark them fixed after the retest
06

Report

An executive summary, every finding with evidence and a ready-to-apply fix, and the standards referenced.

STEPS

  1. Read the summary
  2. Export it as Markdown
  3. Deliver, then retest
03Tips
  • Tests are run only on apps you own, with written authorization.
  • Write access is proven, then rolled back; no data is changed.
  • The demo data in the console is fictional.
  • An automated scan sold for under $100 is not a penetration test.
04FAQ
Will testing break my app?

No. Destructive actions are out of scope, and any write is rolled back.

My app is only a prototype. Does it need a test?

If it is live and stores anyone's email or booking, yes.

What do I receive?

A report with a summary, each finding scored with evidence and a fix, and a free retest.

Who runs the tests?

A certified infrastructure engineer at Lemon Network Solutions, Maryland.
